transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Well... my husband wanted me to come in. It's... it's about the house. The kitchen, mostly. 

For nearly two years now, I've just been sure that the contractor and... well, some of the people on my block... they're quietly working together to cheat us. They're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose. My husband keeps showing me receipts, and they give all these excuses, but... I know what's going on. So, I guess that's why I'm here.
Do any of the people you live with or spend a lot of time with believe this same thing about the contractor and your neighbors?
No... I don't think so. My husband certainly doesn't. He... well, he just doesn't see it. And I don't really talk to anyone else about it.
Has anyone else ever told you they believe the contractor and neighbors are trying to cheat you too?
No. Like I said, I don't really talk about it with anyone else. So... no one has said that to me.
Have you ever had the feeling that your thoughts were being put into your mind by someone else or taken out of your mind?
No. I... no, that's not something that happens to me. My thoughts are my own.
Besides the kitchen and contractor, have you had any other unusual beliefs that other people say are not true?
No... I don't. It's just the situation with the kitchen. There isn't anything else.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people could not, like voices when no one is there?
No. I... no. I don't hear voices or see things. Nothing like that.
Have you had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable?
No. I... no, I don't get like that. I just have my regular energy. Nothing unusual.
Have you been using any drugs, alcohol, or new medications around the time this belief started?
No. I don't drink. And... no drugs. Just my usual pills for my blood pressure, same as always. Nothing new.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion centered on the contractor/neighbors cheating her about the kitchen for nearly two years, with no hallucinations, no thought insertion/broadcasting, no mood episode, and no substance or medication trigger. The presentation is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder (F22) rather than an organic delusional disorder (F06.2), as no evidence of a medical/neurologic cause was elicited.
